p.intro1: It's the morning of your 17th birthday in Paisapur, a small town outside Hyderabad.
p.intro2: Downstairs, someone is humming. It smells like fresh parathas.
p.mom_prof: Professor Arth called this morning. He wants to see you at his Money Lab, across the square, to the north-west. Go on!
p.prof1: Ah, {name}! Happy birthday! Come in, come in.
p.prof2: I am Professor Arth. I study the most powerful force in Paisapur. Not electricity. Not cricket. MONEY!
p.prof3: Every young person in this town gets a Money Journal on their 17th birthday. But first, tell me about the life you're living.
p.q_look: First things first: which of these is you?
p.q_stage: Are you still in school, or already at college?
p.q_source: And where does your money come from each month?
p.prof_income: That's your income: the money that comes in. Some income is fixed, some changes every month. Planning starts with knowing yours.
p.q_goal: Now, the fun part. What's your big goal this year?
p.prof_goal: A {goalName} for ₹{target}! A goal with a number and a deadline is a plan. A goal without one is a wish.
p.prof_gift: Here is your Money Journal. Every money idea you learn gets written in it. And here's ₹1,000 to start your year.
p.kabir1: Professor! Did I miss it? Oh, hey {name}! Happy birthday, friend!
p.prof_kabir: Kabir, right on time, as usual. (He was not.) Here's your Journal and your ₹1,000.
p.kabir2: ₹1,000! I'm going to double it by next week. Easy. See you around, {name}!
p.prof_bank: Hmm. Doubling money in a week... we'll see. {name}, keeping cash at home is risky. Your first step: open an account at Paisapur Bank, east of my lab.
p.prof_controls: Press A to talk to people and read signs. Press MENU to see your Journal, wallet and badges. Off you go!
p.goal_quick: Small and soon! If you save steadily you could have it within a few months, without borrowing a rupee.
p.goal_education: Spending on learning can pay you back for the rest of your life. Let's make sure it doesn't come with a debt that hurts.
p.goal_asset: A stall of your own! That's an asset: something that can put money in your pocket every month.
p.goal_consumption: Lovely! Remember, though: phones and bikes are worth less every year you own them. Let's not pay extra for them.

c1.prof_hint: Paisapur Bank is just east of here. Meena Rao, the manager, will look after you.
c1.mom_generic: Did you open your bank account yet? Meena Rao at the bank is very kind.
c1.mom_docs: Documents for the bank? Let's look in the cupboard together. Take only what the bank asks for, and keep everything else safe at home.
c1.mom_proud: You opened your own bank account? I'm so proud of you!
c1.mom_buyer: Oh, and someone was asking about your old cycle. They're waiting outside to buy it.
c1.meena1: Welcome to Paisapur Bank! I'm Meena Rao, the branch manager. Here to open your first account?
c1.meena_docs: Wonderful! First we need your KYC documents: a proof of identity, a proof of address and a photo. Bring them and we'll get started.
c1.meena_has_docs: You brought your documents. Let's open your account!
c1.meena_savings: Good choice! A savings account keeps your money safe and pays you interest.
c1.meena_current: A current account is for businesses that make lots of payments, and it pays no interest. Let's open a savings account for you instead.
c1.meena_none: Cash at home doesn't grow, and it can be lost or stolen. Bank deposits are even insured up to ₹5 lakh. Let's open a savings account.
c1.q_deposit: How much of your cash would you like to deposit?
c1.meena_interest: Your account pays 3.5% a year. The bank credits a little interest every month.
c1.meena_card: Here's your debit card. Choose a secret PIN, and never, ever tell it to anyone. Not even me.
c1.meena_upi: Last thing: let's set up UPI on your phone, so you can pay by scanning a QR code.
c1.meena_done: All done! You're officially banked. Go and tell your family!
c1.meena_wait: Your account is ready. Your family will want to hear the news, go and tell them!
c1.meena_challenge: You've been through a lot today! Ready for my challenge? Answer my questions and earn the Banked badge.
c1.meena_pass: Excellent! You know your way around a bank. Here is the Banked badge!
c1.meena_next: Professor Arth will want to hear about this. Go and see him.
c1.meena_fail: Not quite. Check your Money Journal from the MENU and come back when you're ready.
c1.meena_help: Welcome back! What can I do for you?
c1.sms_kyc: SMS from VK-PSPBNK: "Dear customer, your KYC is INCOMPLETE. Your account will be BLOCKED in 2 hours. Update now at bit.ly/pspb-kyc and share the OTP."
c1.sms_click1: You tap the link. It looks just like the bank's page. You type your details and the OTP that arrives.
c1.sms_click2: Ding! "₹500 debited from your account." That wasn't the bank. It was a phishing scam.
c1.sms_call1: A man answers: "Paisapur Bank KYC department. Please tell me the OTP you just received to update your account."
c1.sms_call2: Something feels wrong. You hang up. A number in a scam SMS only leads to the scammer.
c1.sms_ignore: You delete the SMS and ask Meena later. She laughs: "We never send KYC links. Well done!"
c1.buyer1: Hey! You're {name}, right? I heard you're selling your old cycle. I'll buy it for ₹1,500!
c1.buyer2: I'm sending you a QR code on UPI. Just scan it and enter your PIN to RECEIVE the money. Quick, I'm in a hurry!
c1.qr_lost: You scan and enter your PIN. "Paid ₹800 to CycleBuyer." Wait... PAID? Entering your PIN sends money. It never receives it.
c1.qr_refuse: "I don't need a PIN to receive money. Send it to my UPI ID instead," you say.
c1.kabir: I already spent my ₹1,000. Snacks, a game top-up... and some other stuff. It went so fast!
c1.meena_form: “Now the form. Take your time with the nominee line — people rush it and regret it.”

c2.prof1: The Banked badge! Splendid. Now comes the real test: a month. Money arrives, money leaves. First lesson: needs and wants.
c2.prof2: Your income is about ₹{income} a month, and your needs cost about ₹{needs}. The rest is yours to plan. Let's use jars.
c2.prof3: And remember: every rupee can only be spent once.
c2.prof4: Each month: buy the needs on your family's list at Zaroorat Store, then sleep at home to end the month. Shauq Bazaar sells wants. Choose wisely!
c2.prof_pyf1: You survived a whole month! Here's my favourite trick for saving: pay yourself first.
c2.q_autosave: Shall I ask the bank to move some money into your goal pot every month, automatically?
c2.pyf_set: Done! From next month, your saving happens before you can spend it.
c2.pyf_later: As you wish. But at the end of the month, there's usually nothing left to save. Think about it.
c2.prof_hint: Buy your needs each month at Zaroorat Store, then sleep at home. After two months, take Anwar Chacha's challenge.
c2.mom_list: This month's list: bus pass, phone recharge, notebooks, and your share of the groceries. Zaroorat Store has them all.
c2.anwar1: Welcome to Zaroorat Store! I'm Anwar Chacha. Everything on my shelves is something people need.
c2.anwar2: And every bill shows the GST, the tax on what you buy. Look closely at your receipt!
c2.anwar_inflation: You noticed? My prices went up a little again. Not my fault, beta: it's inflation. Everything costs a bit more every year.
c2.anwar_challenge: Two months on a budget! Let's see what you've learnt.
c2.anwar_pass: Shabash! You know the difference between a need and a want. Here's the Budget badge!
c2.anwar_fail: Close, but not yet. Read your Journal and try again.
c2.shauq1: Welcome to Shauq Bazaar! TODAY ONLY: 50% OFF on everything!! (Sign behind the counter: "Today only", dated three months ago.)
c2.kabir1: {name}! These sneakers were ₹3,600, now only ₹1,800! I bought two pairs! You have to get some!
c2.kabir_buy: Yes! Twins! Let's go and pick a colour!
c2.kabir_budget: Check your budget? Boring! ...But wait, how much is left in mine? Uh oh.
c2.kabir_later: I already got my {goalName}! Bought it on a credit card. Pay later, enjoy now, right?
c2.after_month1: Your phone buzzes. A message from Professor Arth: "One month done! Come and see me, I have a trick for saving."
c2.jobs1: Need some extra money? Help me unload the market trucks today and I'll pay you ₹300.
c2.jobs_paid: Good work! Here's ₹300. Come back next month, there's always work.
c2.jobs_done: That's all the work for this month. Come back next month!
c2.prof_plan: Your {goalName} costs ₹{target}. If you save about ₹{save} a month, you could have it in about {goalMonths} months.
c2.prof_whatif: And one more thing: my What-If Machine, by the door, lets you go back to any big decision, try another choice and compare both lives. Mistakes are for learning here!
c2.shauq_emi: Ah, you're saving for a {goalName}? Why wait? Take it home TODAY on a Paisapur credit card! No-cost EMI! Easy!
c2.emi_taken: Enjoy! Your first card bill comes next month. Paying just the minimum is fine... for us.
c2.emi_saved: Suit yourself. ("No-cost" EMIs often hide fees, and if you miss a payment, card interest is over 40% a year.)
c2.pyf_already: You already set aside ₹{autosave} a month in Goal Builder. That's paying yourself first: it leaves your account before you can spend it.

c3.prof_hint: Talk to Lakshmi Aunty in the square. Nobody in Paisapur knows more about saving.
c3.mom: An emergency fund means a broken phone is a bad day, not a disaster.
c3.crack1: CRACK! On the way home, your phone slips out of your pocket at the bus stop.
c3.crack2: The screen is shattered. The repair shop says ₹1,500.
c3.crack_fund: You check your bank balance. You have savings for exactly this kind of day.
c3.crack_nofund: You check your balance. It's not enough. Your stomach drops.
c3.crack_paid: The phone is fixed. Paying for a surprise from savings feels... calm.
c3.crack_mom: Here, take it from me. Pay me back a little each month, okay?
c3.crack_skip: You tape the screen and squint at it for the next few months. It's stressful.
c3.lakshmi1: Hello, dear! I'm Lakshmi Aunty. I run the savings group: thirty women, saving a little every month for years.
c3.lakshmi2: Here's our secret: save early, and let the interest earn interest.
c3.lakshmi3: And a trick to see how fast money grows: divide 72 by the interest rate.
c3.lakshmi4: For money you won't need for a while, there's the fixed deposit. Meena at the bank can open one for you now.
c3.lakshmi5: And here's how I keep score: everything I own minus everything I owe.
c3.lakshmi_ready: You have a proper safety net! Ready for my challenge?
c3.lakshmi_notyet: Build an emergency fund of 3 months of needs in your bank, and keep it for a couple of months. Then come back. Your MENU shows how many months you've saved.
c3.lakshmi_pass: Wonderful! You're a real saver now. Here's the Saver badge!
c3.lakshmi_fail: Not quite, dear. Read your Journal and try again.
c3.lakshmi_later: Save first, spend later, and sleep peacefully!
c3.jobsms: WhatsApp from an unknown number: "PART-TIME JOB! Earn ₹5,000/day just by liking videos! Pay ₹500 registration to start. Only 3 seats left!"
c3.job_paid: You pay ₹500. They send ₹50 for your first task... then ask for ₹2,000 to unlock "premium tasks". You block them, ₹450 poorer.
c3.job_ignore: Real jobs pay you. They never ask you to pay to join. You block and report the number.
c3.kabir1: {name}... can you lend me ₹500? I spent everything on sneakers and I need a bus pass.
c3.kabir_thanks: You're the best! I'll pay you back, I promise.
c3.kabir_no: It's okay, I understand. I'll ask my dad. Again.
c3.kabir_later: I'm trying this budget thing. It's harder than it looks!
c3.prof_scholarship: Good news for a learner like you: the coaching centre gives merit scholarships. Answer my two questions and I'll recommend you!
c3.scholarship_won: Splendid! The centre is giving you ₹1,500. I've put it straight into your goal pot: money you never have to repay.
c3.scholarship_lost: Not this time. Scholarships come round every year, so keep applying, to many of them.
c3.prof_leaks: Before you chase more money, find out where the money you already have is going. Most of it leaves in twenty-rupee pieces.
c3.crack_app: The app pays the repair shop in minutes. The repayments, and the reminders, start next month.
c3.crack_sold: You sell your old cycle to a neighbour to pay for the repair. It hurts a little, but you owe nobody.

c4.prof1: Many people borrow for big things. Borrowing isn't always bad, but there is good debt and bad debt.
c4.prof2: Every loan has a principal, an interest rate and a tenure. The EMI is what you pay each month.
c4.prof3: Compare before you borrow: Mr. Iyer at the bank, the moneylender next to Shauq Bazaar... and stay away from anyone in the back alley.
c4.prof_hint: Compare the bank's loan with the moneylender's. Look at the TOTAL you'd repay, not just the EMI. Then take Mr. Iyer's challenge.
c4.mom: Your uncle took a loan from a moneylender once. It took him three years to get free of it.
c4.iyer1: Good morning. I'm Mr. Iyer, loans officer. Before any bank lends to you, it looks at your credit score.
c4.iyer_hint: Before you decide, compare my rates with the moneylender's. Then come back for my challenge.
c4.iyer_challenge: Let's see if you'd make a wise borrower.
c4.iyer_pass: Very good. You read the fine print. Here's the Smart Borrower badge.
c4.iyer_fail: Not yet. Remember: total cost, not just EMI.
c4.lender1: Need money? I'm quick. No papers, no questions. Cash today.
c4.lender2: Just 5% a month. Small, no? (5% a month is 60% a year.)
c4.shady1: Psst. Need money fast? Install the InstaPaisa app. ₹5,000 in five minutes, no documents! Just allow access to your contacts and photos.
c4.shady_installed: Ha! Money's in your account. Enjoy!
c4.app_terms: The app sent ₹4,000, not ₹5,000: a ₹1,000 "processing fee". You owe ₹5,000 plus 4% a month, over 3 months.
c4.shady_refused: Your loss, kid. (He slinks back into the alley.)
c4.shady_again: Changed your mind? No? Then move along.
c4.call1: Incoming call: "Hello, this is the Paisapur Bank fraud team. Someone is using your debit card right now!"
c4.call2: "To block the card, tell me the OTP we've just sent you. Quickly, before they empty your account!"
c4.call_lost: You read out the OTP. "Thank you, sir." Click. ₹1,000 leaves your account. The real bank never asks for OTPs.
c4.call_hangup: You hang up and call the number on the back of your card. The bank says: there was no fraud, but there was a fraudster. Well done.
c4.harass1: Message from InstaPaisa: "PAY NOW OR WE WILL MESSAGE ALL YOUR CONTACTS." Your friends start getting strange messages about you.
c4.harass2: Predatory loan apps harass borrowers. If this happens, don't panic: report the app to the cybercrime helpline 1930 and tell an adult you trust.
c4.shauq_bnpl: These headphones? Just ₹300 a month! Buy now, pay later with a Paisapur credit card. No money needed today!
c4.card_yes: Enjoy your headphones! Your first card bill comes next month. You can pay just the minimum...
c4.card_no: Suit yourself! (You remember: paying only the minimum on ₹1,200 could take over a year and cost hundreds in interest.)
c4.kabir_repay: Here's the money I owed you. Thanks for trusting me.
c4.kabir1: {name}, I'm in trouble. I took a loan from that InstaPaisa app. I borrowed ₹5,000 and now they want ₹8,000!
c4.kabir2: They're messaging my mom, my cousins, everyone in my contacts. What do I do?
c4.kabir_report: Report it to 1930 and the police, and tell my parents? Okay. Okay. I'll do it today.
c4.kabir_another: Another loan to pay this one? That's... how I got here. Maybe I should talk to my parents instead.
c4.kabir_later: I'm never downloading a loan app again.
c4.prof_already: You already reached your goal by saving, without a single loan. That's rare, and it's worth more than you think.
c4.prof_edu: Your {goalName} is education. A loan for learning that raises what you can earn can be good debt, if the rate is fair. Mr. Iyer has an education loan; try scholarships first.
c4.prof_asset: Your stall would earn about ₹600 a month. Borrowing for something that earns more than its EMI can make sense. Borrowing for something that earns nothing rarely does.
c4.prof_cons: Your {goalName} will be worth less every year. Borrowing for it means paying interest on something that keeps shrinking. Ask yourself: can I wait and save?
c4.prof_quick: Your goal was small enough to save for. That's why you didn't need a loan. Bigger goals are where borrowing tempts people.
c4.iyer_edu: Our education loan charges 0.8% a month, less than our regular loan, and it's meant for courses and study tools.
c4.iyer_wait: Live with your choices for a couple of months: pay your EMIs, see how it feels. Then come back for my challenge.
c4.ladder_family: Two thousand? All right, but you pay it back over three months, beta. I'll be counting.
c4.ladder_bank: The bank? Then go to Mr. Iyer and his papers. Slow, but cheaper than me. I won't pretend otherwise.
c4.ladder_moneylender: Here's your ₹2,000. Five percent a month, every month. I'll see you on the first.
c4.ladder_bnpl: Pay-later is for buying things at Shauq Bazaar. There's nothing to buy here.
c4.ladder_app: You install the app. ₹2,000 lands in your account, out of the ₹2,500 you now owe. The first reminder arrives before you're home.
c4.ladder_none: Not borrowing? Smart. Most people who come here wish they hadn't.

c5.prof1: The Smart Borrower badge! Now let's talk about making money grow. But beware: inflation eats money that just sits.
c5.prof2: Big news! The town is rebuilding the bridge to Deccan City by selling bonds. When you buy a bond, you lend the town money. Visit the Bond Office!
c5.prof_hint: Buy a town bond at the Bond Office. Once the bridge opens, visit the Deccan Exchange and talk to Ravi Sharma.
c5.mom: Your grandmother kept her savings in gold. Your father keeps his in the bank. What will you do?
c5.bond1: Welcome to the Town Bond Office! The bridge to Deccan City needs rebuilding, and the town is borrowing from its citizens.
c5.bond2: Lend the town ₹500 or more for one year, and we'll pay it back with 8% interest. Safe, steady, and you help build a bridge!
c5.bond_menu: Would you like to buy town bonds?
c5.bond_thanks: Thank you! With citizens like you, the bridge will be ready by next month. Get some sleep!
c5.bridge_open: News spreads through Paisapur: the new bridge to Deccan City is open! The Deccan Exchange is just across the river.
c5.ravi1: Welcome to the Deccan Exchange, young one. I'm Ravi Sharma. I've watched these prices for forty years.
c5.ravi2: A share is a small piece of a company. Prices go up and down every day. The trick isn't to guess. It's to be patient.
c5.ravi_menu: What would you like to know?
c5.ravi_funds: Don't want to pick companies? Funds pool everyone's money. An index fund buys ALL the companies, cheaply. An active fund pays someone to pick, and charges more.
c5.ravi_sip: And the best habit: put a fixed amount in every month, rain or shine. That's a SIP. You can set one up at the trading desk.
c5.ravi_long: Money you need soon goes in the bank. Money for many years can ride the waves of the market. And there WILL be waves.
c5.ravi_challenge: Let's see if you've learnt patience.
c5.ravi_pass: Forty years, and I still learn something every day. You've earned the Investor badge.
c5.ravi_fail: Patience, young one. Read your Journal, then come back.
c5.gold1: Gold! Your grandmother's favourite. It keeps its value when other things fall. But it pays no interest, and jewellery has making charges.
c5.plots1: This plot is for sale: ₹50,000. Land can grow in value and earn rent. But it's expensive, and selling it takes months.
c5.plots2: Can't afford it yet? Most people save for years for property. Come back when you're older!
c5.kabir1: {name}! My Telegram group says Gully Gadgets will go 10x! I'm putting everything in. Everything!
c5.kabir_warn: "Everything in one stock because a stranger said so?" ...Too late. I already put it all in. If it falls, I'm in trouble.
c5.kabir_join: Right?! Let's both go all in! (Gully Gadgets falls 40% the next month.)
c5.kabir_later: I'm learning that the people who post tips are usually selling.
c5.ravi_wait: Markets need time, young one. Stay invested a few months, through the ups and the downs, then come back for my challenge.

c6.prof1: Six chapters, five badges! But something is wrong. Everyone in Deccan City is talking about a scheme called "Double Dhamaka".
c6.prof2: Kabir has joined. Half the town has joined. Investigate, {name}. And visit the Insurance Office and the Cyber Cell while you're there.
c6.prof_hint: Find out the truth about Double Dhamaka, then report it to Inspector Fatima at the Cyber Cell.
c6.jackpot1: Welcome, welcome! I'm Mr. Jackpot! Put in ₹2,000 today, get ₹4,000 in 30 days! GUARANTEED!
c6.jackpot2: Everyone's getting paid! Bring three friends and get a bonus! But hurry, the offer closes tonight!
c6.ponzi_in: Wonderful choice! Your money is working very hard. (For him.)
c6.ponzi_ask: "Where do the returns come from?" ... "From, er, SMART TRADING! Very smart! Next question!"
c6.ponzi_think: Guaranteed. Double. Hurry. Bring friends. The early members are paid with the new members' money. It's a Ponzi scheme.
c6.ponzi_leave: Guaranteed returns, pressure to decide tonight, bonuses for recruiting friends. You walk out.
c6.jackpot_again: Changed your mind? Only a few seats left!
c6.jackpot_closed: The office is empty. A police notice is taped to the door.
c6.ins1: Hello! I sell insurance. Thousands of people each pay a small premium, and the pool pays for the few who face a big loss.
c6.ins_q: Would you like to protect your belongings for ₹100 a month?
c6.ins_bought: You're covered! If disaster strikes, you won't face it alone.
c6.ins_no: No problem. I hope you never need it.
c6.ins_have: Your policy is active. ₹100 a month, and peace of mind.
c6.fire1: Smoke rises over Paisapur! A fire at the market destroys the stall where you stored your things.
c6.fire_insured: The insurance company pays for everything. You lost a bad afternoon, not your savings.
c6.fire_uninsured: No insurance. Replacing everything costs ₹2,000 from your savings.
c6.fatima1: Inspector Fatima, Cyber Cell. Most frauds start with someone sharing too much: an ID photo, a password, an OTP.
c6.fatima2: And if you're ever scammed, act fast: call 1930 first, then your bank to block the account, then report on cybercrime.gov.in and change your passwords.
c6.fatima_report: Double Dhamaka? We've had our eye on Mr. Jackpot. With your evidence, we're moving in tonight.
c6.fatima_refund: We recovered some of the money. Here's ₹800 of your ₹2,000. Most victims of a Ponzi get nothing back.
c6.kabir_lost: Later, Kabir finds you. "I lost my money in Double Dhamaka. But I reported it fast, like you said. Thanks, friend."
c6.fatima_challenge: You've helped Paisapur a great deal. One last challenge before I give you the Shield badge.
c6.fatima_pass: Outstanding. Here's the Shield badge. Professor Arth will want to see you.
c6.fatima_fail: Not yet. Review your Journal, then come back.
c6.fatima_hint: We've heard rumours about a get-rich scheme across the road. If you learn anything, report it here.
c6.fatima_done: Stay sharp, and keep your PINs to yourself!
c6.kabir: From now on, I'm doing it your way. Boring. Slow. Safe. Actually... kind of nice.
c6.fire_stall: Your stall burns down! Without insurance, rebuilding and restocking costs ₹4,000 from your savings.
c6.fatima_rescue: Kabir is outside, shaking. Help him do the right things, in the right order. The first hour matters most.

end.prof1: {name}! Six badges. A full Money Journal. Do you remember when you came in here a year ago, with ₹1,000 and a birthday cake?
end.prof2: One more lesson for the road: when you start earning more, part of your income goes to the government as tax. That's how roads and schools get built.
end.prof3: Life is long, and money is a tool. Use it well, {name}. Come back any time: the Journal is always here.

town.bridge_before: That bridge collapsed in the floods years ago. The town can't afford to rebuild it... yet.
town.bridge_after: Thanks to the bonds, we have our bridge back! My grandson works in Deccan City now.
town.auntie1: I keep my savings in the bank AND a little gold, like my mother did. Never all in one place!
town.auntie2: Did you hear? Someone in our lane lost money to a phone call pretending to be the bank. Hang up on those!
town.city: Deccan City moves fast. Don't let anyone rush you into a money decision.
town.trader: I put everything into Gully Gadgets after a tip in a chat group. It's down 40%. Never again.

common.bed_early: It's the middle of the day! There's too much to do.
common.bed_needs: You haven't bought everything on this month's needs list. If you sleep now, you'll go without.
common.shelf: Your old piggy bank. Money in a piggy bank just sits there; money in the bank earns interest.
common.overwhelmed1: Everything feels like too much. The bills, the debts, the worry. You sit down on the floor.
common.overwhelmed2: Hey. Sit with me. We'll sort this out together. Here's ₹1,000 to get you through.
common.overwhelmed3: Next time, keep a little aside for bad days. That's what an emergency fund is for.
common.mom_borrow: You need some money? All right. Pay me back a little each month. No interest, but I'll be keeping count!
common.mom_borrow_yes: There. And {name}: a debt to family is still a debt.
common.atm_no: An ATM. You need a bank account to use it.
common.terminal: The lab computer shows your Money Journal.
common.books: A row of books: "Compound Interest: The Eighth Wonder", "Needs, Wants and Sneakers", "Don't Click That Link".

goal.already: You've already reached this goal. Pick a new one from Professor Arth's list, or enjoy it!
goal.bought_saved: It's yours, paid for with money you saved. No EMIs, no interest, no worry. That's what waiting buys you.
goal.bought_loan: It's yours! But remember: part of it is still borrowed money, and the EMIs continue.
goal.done_asset: Your stall opens next to Anwar Chacha's shop. From next month it earns ₹600 a month: an asset working for you.
goal.done_education: Your course starts next week. Learning is the one thing nobody can take back from you.
goal.done_consumption: Brand new and shiny! From today it starts losing value, which is fine because you didn't borrow for it.
goal.done_quick: Done, and it took only a few months of saving. Imagine what a bigger plan could do.
goal.wait: No rush. Your money stays in your goal pot, earning interest.
goal.not_enough: Your {goalName} costs ₹{target}. You need ₹{goalGap} more. Keep saving: a little every month adds up.
goal.loan_hint: (You could also ask Mr. Iyer about a loan. Compare the total cost first!)
goal.next_intro: Goal reached! Now, what's next? The best savers always have a next goal.
goal.next_set: New goal: a {goalName} for ₹{target}. Your goal pot keeps working towards it.
goal.rest: No new goal for now. Your savings can simply grow as a safety net.

src.festival1: Diwali rush at the family shop! Customers everywhere. Dad hands you ₹1,000 extra for all your help.
src.windfall_q: What will you do with this extra money?
src.windfall_saved: All of it goes into your goal pot. Future you says thank you.
src.windfall_most: ₹700 into the goal pot, ₹300 for a little celebration. A balanced choice.
src.windfall_spent: New clothes, sweets for friends, a movie... it was fun. By next week, the ₹1,000 is gone.
src.lump1: Your college scholarship arrives: ₹3,000 for the whole term, all at once.
src.lump_plan: You keep ₹1,000 handy and move ₹2,000 into your goal pot. The term is long; the money should last it.
src.lump_spent: A new jacket, a trip with friends... ₹2,500 gone in a week. The term has barely started.
src.grocery1: This week, you're in charge of the family groceries. Here's ₹2,000. If you spend less, you keep what's left!
src.grocery_good: You made a list, compared prices per kilo, and skipped the fancy packaging. ₹150 left over. It's yours!
src.grocery_meh: You grabbed the first brand on every shelf. It all fit the budget, just. Nothing left over.
src.grocery_bad: Chips, cold drinks, sweets... and the rice ran out on Thursday. Mom is not impressed.
src.lean_tutoring: Your tutoring students have exams next month and are taking a break. Next month you'll earn only about a third of usual.
src.lean_shop: Monsoon floods the market road. The family shop is quiet, and next month's income will be about half.
src.lean_allowance: Things are tight at home this month. Your allowance next month will be a quarter less. I'm sorry, beta.
src.lean_tip: Income can drop without warning. That's exactly what your emergency fund is for.

whatif.not_ready: A strange machine with dials and a big lever. A note says: "Not yet calibrated. Come back after your first month."
whatif.intro: My What-If Machine! It remembers your big decisions. Go back to one, choose differently, and compare both lives. Same world, same luck, only your choices change.
